title: Fractured Flickers
text: Fractured Flickers is a live-action syndicated half-hour comedy television program produced by Jay Ward, who is otherwise known for cartoons. The pilot film was produced in 1961, but the series was not completed until 1963.

title: Wild Kingdom
text: Wild Kingdom, also known as Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom, is an American documentary television program featuring wildlife and nature. It was originally produced from 1963 until 1988, and it was revived in 2002.

title: The Dakotas
text: The Dakotas is an ABC/Warner Bros. Western television series starring Larry Ward and featuring Jack Elam, Chad Everett, and Michael Greene, broadcast during 1963.

title: The Doctors
text: The Doctors is an American daytime soap opera television series which aired on NBC from April 1, 1963, to December 31, 1982.

title: General Hospital
text: General Hospital is an American daytime television soap opera created by Frank and Doris Hursley which has been broadcast on ABC since April 1, 1963. Originally a half-hour serial, its running time was expanded from 30 minutes to 45 minutes on July 26, 1976, and again to a full hour on January 16, 1978.

title: You Don't Say!
text: You Don't Say! is an American television game show.

title: Hootenanny
text: Hootenanny is an American musical variety television show broadcast on ABC from April 1963 to September 1964. The program was hosted by Jack Linkletter.

title: Vacation Playhouse
text: Vacation Playhouse is an American anthology television series that was broadcast on CBS during the summer months from 1963 through 1967.

title: The Lieutenant
text: The Lieutenant is an American television series, created by Gene Roddenberry. An hour-long drama, it aired on NBC on Saturday evenings in the 1963–1964 television schedule.

title: Arrest and Trial
text: Arrest and Trial is a 90-minute American crime/legal drama series that ran during the 1963–1964 season on ABC, airing Sundays from 8:30-10 pm Eastern.

title: Grindl
text: Grindl is an American situation comedy that began in fall 1963 on NBC, originally sponsored by Procter & Gamble. The show, starring Imogene Coca in the title role, lasted for one season.

title: Breaking Point
text: Breaking Point is an American medical drama that aired on ABC from September 16, 1963, to April 27, 1964, with reruns continuing until September 7, 1964. The series, which was a spin-off of Ben Casey, starred Paul Richards and Eduard Franz.

title: The Outer Limits
text: The Outer Limits is an American anthology television series created by Leslie Stevens, that was broadcast on ABC from September 16, 1963, to January 16, 1965. It is often compared to The Twilight Zone, but features a greater emphasis on science fiction.

title: The Fugitive
text: The Fugitive is an American crime drama television series created by Roy Huggins and produced by QM Productions and United Artists Television. It aired on ABC from September 17, 1963, to August 29, 1967.

title: The Greatest Show on Earth
text: The Greatest Show on Earth is an American drama series starring Jack Palance about the American circus, which aired on ABC from September 17, 1963, to September 8, 1964. It was produced by Desilu, the production company founded by Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz.
wiki: The Greatest Show on Earth (TV series)

title: Channing
text: Channing is an hour-long American drama series that aired on Wednesdays at 10:00 p.m. on ABC from September 18, 1963 to April 8, 1964.

title: The Patty Duke Show
text: The Patty Duke Show is an American television sitcom created by Sidney Sheldon and William Asher. The series ran on ABC from September 18, 1963, to April 27, 1966.

title: The Jimmy Dean Show
text: The Jimmy Dean Show is the name of several similar music and variety series on American local and network television between 1963 and 1975. Each starred country music singer Jimmy Dean as host.

title: Temple Houston
text: Temple Houston is an American Western television series starring Jeffrey Hunter as real-life 19th-century Texas lawyer Temple Lea Houston. It ran for one season on NBC from 1963 to 1964.

title: Burke's Law
text: Burke's Law is an American detective television series that aired on ABC from 1963 to 1966. The show starred Gene Barry as millionaire captain of the Los Angeles Police Department's homicide division Amos Burke, who is chauffeured around to solve crimes in his 1962 Rolls-Royce Silver Cloud II complete with an early car phone.

title: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa is exhibited in the United States for the first (and only) time, for a period of four weeks, at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C. During this time it was viewed by over half a million people.
text: Leonardo di ser Piero da Vinci, better known as Leonardo da Vinci, was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance who was active as a painter, draughtsman, engineer, scientist, anatomist, sculptor, and architect. title: The David Mirvish Gallery is opened in Toronto by David Mirvish.
text: David Mirvish, is a Canadian theatre producer, impresario, and art collector. He owns and operates Toronto-based theatrical production company Mirvish Productions, which he founded with his father in 1986.

title: Museum of Contemporary Art (Skopje) opens in Yugoslavia.
text: The Contemporary Art Museum is a contemporary art museum located in Skopje, North Macedonia. It is the biggest and most modern museum in the country.

title: First Pirelli Calendar (for 1964), photographed by Robert Freeman in Mallorca, issued in the United Kingdom. His portrait of The Beatles is used on the cover of their album With the Beatles (released November 22).
text: The Beatles were an English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960. The band comprised John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr.
